description_en: Dathu Bāhāḥ is a branch of Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra, Oku Bāhāḥ (LAL2260) and was built by Kumāraju Śākya in 1678 CE. It is named ‘Dathu’ Bāhāḥ because it is situated in the middle (‘dathu’ in Newari) of twobāhāḥs: Tvāya Bāhāḥ (LAL1840) and Nugaḥ Nhū Bāhāḥ (LAL1820). The members of the Mahābū clan from Oku Bāhāḥ operate thisbāhāḥ. Dathu Bāhāḥ faces west and the two-storey monastic building (kvāḥpāḥchẽ) is covered with corrugated pewter sheets (jastāpātā) and the roof is supported by the plain wooden struts. The main sanctum (garbhagṛha) is on the ground floor while theāgaṃ(shrine of the principal deity) is located on the first floor of thekvāḥpāḥch̃e. Instead of atoraṇa,the main entrance to the sanctum features wooden carvings of Prajñāpāramitā and Lokeśvara, symbolizing the Triratnas (Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha).A Svayambhūcaityaand a well are built in the Bāhāḥ’s premises.Kumāraju Śākya[3]commissioned the initial construction of this Bāhāḥ on the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha (Śrīpañcamī) in 1678 CE (798 NS) during the joint reign of King Śrīnivāsa and Yoganarendra Malla.[4]During the initial construction, statues of Akṣobhya, Cakrasaṃvara-Vajravārāhī, Gaṇeśa, Mahākāl, and a Svayambhū Caitya were also installed in the Bāhāḥ’s premises. The first floor of thekvāḥpāḥchẽwas damaged during the 1934 CE earthquakes and was repaired by the Bāhāḥsaṅghamembers. Thekvāpāḥchẽwas again severely affected by the 2015 CE earthquakes.Four families from the Mahābū clan living in Oku Bāhāḥ carry out the daily rituals in this Bāhāḥ.[5]The anniversary of the Svayambhū Caitya installed in the Bāhāḥ’s premises takes place on the fifth of the bright fortnight of Māgha (Śrīpañcamī).Footnotes^^Thekvāḥpāḥchẽ’s roof is covered by corrugated pewter sheets (jastāpātā) and is supported by the plain wooden struts.^Since some part of the inscription recording the initial construction of Dathu Bāhāḥ is broken now, this name is taken from Pruscha (1975, P-183).^Kumāraju Śākya was a younger brother of Amṛtavajra Śākya, who commissioned Nugaḥ Nhū Bāhāḥ (LAL1820) in 1643 CE (NS 763). He named Dathu Bāhāḥ as Amṛtavarṇa Mahāvihāra (in Sanskrit) after his brother’s name.^Each family is responsible to carry out these rituals for one month.
description_ne: यो ओकु बाहा:को शाखा विहार हो । त्वाय् बाहा: (LAL1840) र  नुग: न्हू बाहा: (LAL1820) को बीचमा रहेको हुनाले यसको नाम दथु बाहा: रहेको हो । ओकु बाहा: (LAL2260) का महाबू खलकका सदस्यहरूले यो बाहा: सञ्चालन गरिरहेका छन् । पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको दुई तलाको यो बाहा:को क्वा:पा:छेँको छानामा जस्तापाता राखिएको छ । छानाको भार थाम्न सादा टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । क्वा:पा:छेँको पहिलो तलामा आगम राखिएको छ भने भुइँतलामा गर्भगृह बनाइएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि तोरण राखिएको छैन तर ढोकाको माथिल्लो भागमा बुद्ध, धर्म, संघको प्रतीक स्वरूप बीचमा अक्षोभ्य राखी दायाँ-बायाँ प्रज्ञापारमिता र लोकेश्वर राखिएका छन् । यहाँको क्वा:पा:छेँको पेटीमा सिंह राखिएका छैनन् । बाहा: प्रङ्गनमा एउटा स्वयम्भू चैत्य र इनार स्थापना गरिएका छन् ।यो बाहा: नेसं ७९८ (सन् १६७८) माघ शुक्ल ५ (श्रीपञ्चमी) को दिनमा श्रीनिवास मल्ल र योगनरेन्द्र मल्लको संयुक्त शासनकालमा कुमारजु शाक्यले स्थापना गरेका थिए । बाहा: स्थापना गर्दा अक्षोभ्य, चक्रसम्वर-वज्रवाराही, गणेश, महाकाल लगायत प्राङ्गनमा स्वयम्भू चैत्य पनि स्थापना गरिएका थिए । यी कुमारजु शाक्य नुग: न्हू बाहा: (LAL1820) स्थापना गर्ने अमृतवज्र शाक्यका भाइ थिए । दाजु अमृतवज्रले नेसं ७६३ (सन् १६४३) मा न्हू बाहा: स्थापना गरेको ३५ वर्षपछि भाइ कुमारजु शाक्य[1]ले पनि यो दथु बाहा: स्थापना गरेका थिए । तर कुमारजु शाक्यले बाहा:को नामाकरण गर्दा आफ्नो नाम नराखी दाजुकै नाममा अमृतवर्ण महाविहार राखेका थिए । विसं १९९० को भूकम्पले क्वा:पा:छेँको पहिलो तला भत्केपछि बाहा:का संघ सदस्यहरूले नै मर्मत गरेका थिए । विसं २०७२ को भूकम्पले क्वापा:छेँमा क्षति पुगेको छ ।ओकु बाहा:को महाबू खलकका चारवटा परिवारले मिलेर एक-एक महिनाको पालो मिलाएर बाहा:को नित्यपूजा चलाइरहेका छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष माघ शुक्ल ५ (श्रीपञ्चमी) को दिनमा क्वा:पा:द्य: र प्राङ्गनमा रहेको स्वयम्भू चैत्यको वर्षबन्धन पूजा गरिन्छ ।Footnotes^अहिले शिलापत्रको केही ठाउँमा फुटेकोले बाहा: निर्माताको नाम देखिँदैन । यो नामPruscha(1975, P-183) बाट लिइएको हो ।
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)

historical_events.event_description: Kumāraju Śākya commissioned the construction of thebāhāḥon the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha (Śrīpañcamī) in 1678 CE (798 NS) during the joint reign of King Śrīnivāsa and Yoganarendra Malla. During the initial construction, a statue of Akṣobhya was installed in the sanctum as thebāhāh’s primary deity (kvāḥpāḥdyaḥ), and the statues of Cakrasaṃvara-Vajravārāhī, Gaṇeśa and Mahākāla were installed inside theāgaṃ.

historical_events.event_name: Damage during the 1934 CE earthquakes and repair
historical_events.event_description: The first floor of thekvāḥpāḥchẽwas damaged during the 1934 CE earthquakes and was repaired by the Bāhāḥsaṅghamembers.
Some of thekvāḥpāḥchẽhas considerable cracks. Thesaṅghamembers are struggling to receive financial aid for the repair work.
